title: Upper Deck Seat Track Attachment Fitting Change to Titanium

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Replacement of the aluminium seat track attachment lugs on the upper deck by machined titanium items, ending the galvanic pairing that drove corrosion at the track-to-beam interface after the sealed track standard was introduced.

sections.reason: The sealed seat track standard stopped fluid reaching the fastener holes but did not stop corrosion at the interface between the track and the floor beam upper flange. Reports from eleven operators showed the attack had simply moved to the attachment lug, where the aluminium lug, the steel fastener and the sealing compound formed a galvanic couple that the seal made worse by holding moisture against the joint. Fourteen aircraft required lug replacement within four years of the sealed track being embodied, which was well inside the interval the sealed standard was meant to achieve.
sections.description: The aluminium attachment lugs at every upper deck seat track station are replaced by machined titanium items D5350006194262 of identical external envelope but increased flange thickness at the fastener land. The upper floor structure frame D5350004793026 is retained and is re-drilled at the lug positions to a wet-installed pattern, and tension bolts LN231128K9 replace the original fastener set. The sealed track web ARD386097-40 introduced by the previous standard is reused where its condition allows and is otherwise renewed; clevis pins LN666073-13 at the splice positions are always renewed. Faying surfaces receive a glass fibre isolation layer before assembly. Work is carried out from the cabin side in zones 242, 265 and 971 with the seats, the monuments and the floor panels removed. Revised detail is on drawing D53501208297.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 4.9 kg per aircraft over the previous standard, symmetric about the centre line, with a negligible centre-of-gravity effect. No electrical load change. The titanium lug is one-way interchangeable: an aircraft at the titanium standard may not be reverted, but a mixed installation across different track stations is acceptable because each station is a separate load path. The repeat corrosion inspection of the upper deck wet areas may be dropped once the change is embodied on all stations of a deck. Illustrated parts content and the seat installation task both require update.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only. Typical elapsed time is six days when the cabin is already stripped for other work and eleven days otherwise. Kits are held against the same reference for spares, since individual lugs are replaced on condition between campaigns.

type_data.balance_impact: Symmetric installation, CG shift below 0.01 % MAC
type_data.production_impact: No production cut-in proposed; the affected build standard had already left the line
